answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, the 22-miler no longer fits. It would land on Sun Oct 4, 14 days before the race, and you would still be paying for it in race week.

At your long-run pace, 22 miles is about 3 hours 40 minutes. That is well past the 3-hour mark where extra time on your feet adds more fatigue than fitness.

You have the 20 from Sep 13 and the 17 from last Sunday. An 18 with 5 miles at marathon pace gives you the race-pace practice a 22 at easy pace would not, and you recover from it in time.

new.analysis:
## How the week went

You ran last week exactly as planned, and that is the main reason the race move is manageable. All five runs and both rest days matched the plan: 42 miles, pain 0/10 every day, and easy runs steady at about 9:52/mi with heart rate near 138. That is two clean weeks in a row after the overload in the week of Sep 7.

Your threshold work supports a go at under 3:45. You held 7:58/mi across three 2-mile reps with only a 1% fade. Your earlier marathon-pace work came out at 8:35, within a second of the 8:34 you need.

The 61% easy share is lower than the 80% target, but the cause is clear. The threshold session adds hard time through its warm-up and recoveries. The long run also spent 57% of its time in zone 3 even though the pace never changed, so it was sitting at the top of your easy range.

The new date makes this the last week of real work. The race is two weeks after this week ends, so the taper starts now: volume dips slightly, Wednesday loses a rep, and Sunday carries the one big effort left. Expect next week to drop to about 30 miles with a 12-mile long run and one short threshold session. Race week will be short easy runs with a few strides.

Feeling anxious about a moved date makes sense, but nothing in your training shows a gap. Fitness changes very little in the last three weeks, while freshness changes a lot. Your job now is to arrive rested, so keep your two strength sessions light and away from the day before the long run.
